speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Ms Sim Ann and the Acting Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal will subsequently deliver their Ministerial Statements addressing related issues.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Israeli conduct of the war in Gaza and the other actions they have taken in the West Bank has sparked renewed efforts by the international community to press Israel to change course.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This resolution reflected widespread concern that the two-state solution is being eroded by Israel’s actions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Around 10 countries may announce recognition of Palestine later today at the UN.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For some of them, the recognition will be conditional, predicated on the Palestinian Authority's commitment to renounce terrorism and to conduct administrative reform.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They also expect, perhaps wishfully, for Hamas to disarm and to release all the hostages.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I will now lay out Singapore’s position on the recognition of Palestinian statehood.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Allow me to start by setting out Singapore's national interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore is a multiracial, multi-religious city state in the heart of Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Given our circumstances, that means we have three priorities.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The long-standing complicated tragedy of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict elicits strong and diverse reactions amongst Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we must express these different perspectives respectfully.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We cannot allow external events or actors to cause fissures in our society.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: National policies and especially, foreign policy positions, must be based on Singapore's national interests and not on communal or religious perspectives; and we must never allow outsiders to exploit potential domestic fissures within our own society.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must never be complacent about the threat of terrorism and military conflict.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As a small and open nation, we cannot condone terrorism in any form.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We must never accept any excuse or any justification for the wanton killing of innocent civilians and the taking of hostages.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Actually, whenever a terrorist incident occurs overseas, the questions that go through my mind are the following: "What if this had happened in Singapore?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What actions would our military and security agencies have to undertake?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What would our diplomats say the next day at the United Nations?" This is why we supported Israel's right of self-defence after the 7 October terrorist attacks, because if anything similar were to ever happen in Singapore, have no doubt, we would assert the same right of self-defence.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also, for the sake of our security, need to maintain cooperation with international partners.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is to enhance our defence and our security capabilities and to keep Singapore safe.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We all know that Israel helped us to build up the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) in our earliest years of Independence, when we were most vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This unique security relationship remains invaluable to us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But this does not stop us from conveying our views directly to the Israeli government, clearly and constructively, when we do not agree with their actions.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have done so and we will continue to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The third is promoting respect for and compliance with international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore relies on clear rules and norms to safeguard our sovereignty as a tiny city state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A world based on "might is right" is fundamentally inimical to small states like us.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, it means Singapore must abide by and uphold international law consistently.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: These three priorities surrounding our national interests have shaped our approach to the conflict in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On 7 October 2023 itself, Singapore immediately condemned the terrorist attack on Israel by Hamas and we recognised Israel's right of self-defence, in accordance with international law and the United Nations (UN) Charter.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have always and repeatedly called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But in exercising its right to defend itself, Israel must comply with international humanitarian law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: That includes the principle of proportionality in warfare.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And our view is that Israel's actions in Gaza have gone too far, for too long.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Israel's military operations, which have recently intensified in Gaza City, have exacerbated the prolonged, desperate suffering of innocent civilians.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Schools, hospitals, places of worship have been struck.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Around 1.9 million or 90% of Gazans have been internally displaced.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Gaza is dangerously close to famine levels and this was entirely preventable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have all seen the heart wrenching pictures of Gazans, including young children scavenging for food.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The deliberate and unlawful denial of humanitarian aid to a civilian population is completely unacceptable.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In our view, these excessive actions by the Israel government may even be a breach of international humanitarian law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This matter is currently before the International Court of Justice, which is the appropriate forum to adjudicate such grave concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In recent weeks, more aid, including from Singapore, has entered Gaza, but this is still woefully inadequate.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It must lift all restrictions on its delivery and to allow the full and unimpeded flow of humanitarian aid.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Palestinians must be enabled to access this aid safely and with dignity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This includes the latest contribution by the Singapore Red Cross of about $1.2 million through the Egyptian Red Crescent, which was just announced during President Tharman Shanmugaratnam's State Visit to Egypt.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last month, SAF air-dropped urgent humanitarian aid to the Palestinians.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, this was the second air-drop operation conducted by SAF.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are grateful to our SAF Servicemen and women for stepping up to do this, to express our compassion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And under our tenth tranche, we will support the following.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, right now, a team of Singaporean doctors and clinicians are currently in Cairo to support the Nasser Institute in case consultations, for the more complicated cases.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The SAF has deployed two liaison officers, based in Cairo, to coordinate Singapore's assistance in-theatre.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are working to deploy another medical team to Egypt to help treat even more patients from Gaza, when the conditions are conducive.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will provide prosthetics supplies for about 100 Palestinian amputees who are being treated in Jordan and in Jordanian field hospitals in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Third, the World Food Programme's efforts to fight hunger in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will continue to support international efforts in the day-after scenarios, including through the Arab Reconstruction Plan.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is too early for specifics, but we will contribute financially and in-kind.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But there needs, first, to be a permanent ceasefire and the hostages must be released unconditionally.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Only then can physical reconstruction and healing begin.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will study any UNSC resolution on this issue carefully and we will assess how we can support its implementation if it comes to pass in future.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Allow me to take you through a brief review of history to put this position in context.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The two-state solution arose in 1947, when the UN General Assembly recommended the partition of the British Mandate of Palestine into separate Arab and Jewish states.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Jerusalem, under this same resolution, was supposed to be a separate, internationally administered entity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Unfortunately, the decades since then, have been littered with missed opportunities by both sides.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For instance, the two-state formulation was accepted by the Jewish leadership in 1947 but rejected by the Arabs.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Jewish leadership took what was on the table, declared Independence, war broke out in 1948.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, it is only in November 1988 did the Palestinian Liberation Organization (PLO) implicitly accept Israel's right to exist.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This is back in 1988 and they proclaimed the State of Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And Singapore welcomed this Proclamation is because we viewed it as significant progress towards a two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Unfortunately, notwithstanding the Oslo Accords in 1993 and 1995, none of the subsequent attempts to reach a final status agreement succeeded.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In January 2006, Hamas won the Palestinian Legislative Council elections and its leader, Ismail Haniyeh, formed the government on the basis of a majority.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But this was largely rejected by the international community, given Hamas' refusal to recognise Israel's right to exist, its rejection of peaceful co-existence and its propagation of terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In June 2007, Hamas violently seized Gaza from the Fatah-dominated Palestinian Authority and has ruled in Gaza by force ever since then and there have been no elections in the Occupied Palestinian Territories for two decades.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: First, whilst the Palestinian Authority administers the Occupied Palestinian Territories in the West Bank, it does not de facto control Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: For the last 18 years at least, there has not been a unified Palestinian government that exercises effective control in Palestinian Territories, including the West Bank and Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: What will happen in Gaza after the ceasefire remains unclear.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Second point, Hamas has consistently rejected Israel's right to exist.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It has yet to renounce terrorism or agree to disarm.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In fact, Hamas has vowed to repeat the terrorist attacks of 7 October, if given the opportunity again.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On the other hand, Singapore enjoys good relations with the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We welcome its commitment to renounce terrorism, to carry out reforms and to disarm Hamas, as President Mahmoud Abbas stated in his letter to French President Emmanuel Macron in June this year.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: However, it remains to be seen whether the Palestinian Authority can really disarm and displace Hamas from Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We can hope, but hope, on its own, is not a reality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we will closely monitor the fulfilment of these commitments made by the Palestinian Authority.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ultimately, to resolve this longstanding conflict in a comprehensive, just and durable manner, there needs to be a negotiated settlement which results in two states, one Israeli, one Palestinian, with their peoples living alongside each other in peace, security and dignity.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As difficult and distant as it may now seem, nevertheless, we believe this is still the only viable pathway to a lasting peace.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore will continue to support any initiative to resume negotiations between the parties involved towards this ultimate goal.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our position should not come as a surprise to people within this House and to our citizens outside Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has consistently affirmed the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and their own state.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our voting record at the United Nations (UN) consistently reflects this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Last year, we voted in favour of several resolutions which expressed support for the admission of Palestine as a UN member and affirmed the Palestinians' right to self-determination.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have also supported Palestine's right to be a "non-member observer state" in various international organisations, including the International Labour Organization and the Universal Postal Union, just to cite some examples.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, what are the prospects for a two-state solution?

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Regrettably, extremist elements on both sides continue to actively undermine the prospects for a two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Hamas has consistently said, "No." At the same time, there are Israeli settlers who continue to displace Palestinians in the West Bank.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Some Israeli politicians have spoken explicitly about annexing parts of the West Bank or Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Recently, the Israeli government signed an agreement to proceed with the so-called E1 settlement project in the West Bank.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This will fragment the West Bank and threaten the contiguity of Arab towns in the Occupied Palestinian Territories even further.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore has consistently held that Israeli settlements are illegal under international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have voted in support of UN resolutions that reject Israeli settlement activities and we have called on Israel to rescind all unilateral measures seeking to change the status of Jerusalem.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We call on the Israeli government to cease settlement construction and expansion.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We oppose ongoing attempts to create new facts on the ground which undermine the prospects for a two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Details will be announced at a later date.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the case of Palestine, this is what we meant when we said that there is a need for an effective Palestinian government that accepts Israel's right to exist and categorically renounces terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This has also been the prevailing view amongst many countries that see recognition as a meaningful step towards the ultimate goal of a negotiated two-state solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But yesterday and today, a few countries have chosen to change their position and to formally recognise the Palestinian state now, even as the prospects of a functioning state have in fact become more remote.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They do so precisely to express their grave concern at the status quo and they hope that this will make it harder for Israel to extinguish a two-state solution altogether.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore, so far, has maintained our position while doing as much as we can to help the Palestinian Authority strengthen their capabilities for future statehood.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore's support for a two-state solution means we will oppose any steps by Israel to extinguish or undermine such a solution.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singapore cannot recognise any unilateral annexation of occupied territory because this would be a flagrant breach of international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: In the meantime, Singapore will step up concrete, constructive support for the Palestinians in preparation for their eventual statehood.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to support the Palestinian Authority's capacity-building efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will offer more scholarships for Palestinian students as well as community policing and leadership programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We established a Representative Office in Ramallah in 2022, which has been a focal point for our capacity-building efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have to continue engaging both the Palestinian Authority and Israel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I know there have been calls to cut diplomatic ties, but doing so would diminish our ability to communicate with Israel and, frankly, serve no practical purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Diplomacy is not just about engaging when there is agreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: It is arguably even more important when there is disagreement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I told him that Israel's military response had gone on too far, for too long.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The scope and the casualties were beyond what could be justified.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I added that Israel's actions were inimical to its own long-term strategic and security interests.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our links with both sides are useful, not just to get our point across, but also, in a very real way, for facilitating our humanitarian assistance for Palestinians, especially in Gaza.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We have worked with both our Arab regional partners on this as well as with the Israelis, whose concurrence is essential for these efforts on the ground.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim has asked about our efforts to ensure that Israel abides by international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: When principles are breached, we speak our mind clearly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to call out actions by all and any side, including by the Israelis or Hamas, that breach international law.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The Israeli people and the Palestinian people both exist as an objective reality.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Both have claims to a sovereign state in their ancestral homeland.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: There can be no "river to the sea" for either side, because if you really try to effect that, some terrible consequences follow from that logically.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: (In Mandarin): Mr Speaker, following Minister Vivian Balakrishnans Ministerial Statement on Singapore's position on the situation in the Middle East, I wish to address the same topic in Mandarin.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I last did so during the 2024 Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There was a need to do so, because the diverse composition of Singapore's society means that different groups have different degrees of awareness and interest in the matter.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Some see the Israel-Hamas conflict as one that has a long and complex history, and very distant from Singapore, while others care deeply about the fate of Palestine, particularly the pain and suffering of civilians in Gaza, and have strong views about the foreign policy stance Singapore should take.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is why the Middle East situation has been featured in many Parliamentary Questions, as well as a dedicated debate in Parliament.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It has the potential to trigger disagreements, even intense disputes, on social media as well as political platforms.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: If not handled well, it can also affect our social unity.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Hence, the Government has been explaining our approach and position carefully.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore immediately condemned the terrorist attacks on Israel by Hamas on 7 October 2023, and recognised Israel's right to self-defence in accordance with international law and the UN Charter.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have always and repeatedly called for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages taken by Hamas.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have called out Israel's actions in Gaza, which have gone too far for too long.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Israel's military operations have exacerbated the prolonged, desperate suffering of innocent civilians.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore will continue to do what we can to contribute to international efforts to alleviate civilian suffering in Gaza.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore believes that a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, is the only viable pathway to a comprehensive, just, and durable solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As a friend of both the Israeli and Palestinian peoples, we hope that they will be able to live side-by-side in peace, security and dignity one day.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In recent months, the situation in the Middle East has become more dire, despite the attempts of multiple countries to mediate and bring about a ceasefire.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Schools, hospitals and places of worship have been struck; medical services are incapacitated and overwhelmed.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Gaza is dangerously close to famine levels, which was entirely preventable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The matter is now before the International Court of Justice.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: These events have further upset those who have been closely following the situation, including some Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As a multiracial and multireligious country situated in the heart of Southeast Asia, our national interests dictate that we have three priorities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I have explained earlier why the issue can impact national unity.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: While Singaporeans may have strong and diverse reactions to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, it is essential for us to express our viewpoints respectfully and be open to different perspectives.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: National policies, especially foreign policy positions, must be based on Singapore’s national interests and not on communal or religious perspectives.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We cannot allow external events and actors to cause fissures in our society or exploit potential fissures in our society.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As a small and open nation, we cannot condone terrorism in any form.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We had supported Israel's right of self-defence after the 7 October terrorist attacks, because if something similar happened to Singapore, we would certainly assert that same right.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We also need to maintain cooperation with international partners to enhance our defence and security capabilities and to keep Singapore safe.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Israel helped us build up the SAF in our early years of independence when we were most vulnerable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This unique security relationship remains invaluable to us.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But this does not stop us from conveying our views directly to the Israeli government, clearly and respectfully, when we do not agree with their actions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have done so and will continue to do so.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The third, is promoting respect for, and compliance with, international law.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A world based on "might is right" is fundamentally inimical to small states.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singaporeans are very familiar with the reasons why.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Hence, we spoke up and said that the deliberate and unlawful denial of humanitarian aid to a civilian population is completely unacceptable.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In our view, the excessive actions by the Israel government may even be a breach of international humanitarian law.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore will continue to do what we can to contribute to international efforts to alleviate civilian suffering in Gaza.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Under our tenth tranche of aid, we will: First, support Egyptian hospitals in treating injured Palestinians.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Second, support Jordan’s Restoring Hope Initiative, which will provide prosthetics supplies for about 100 Palestinian amputees being treated in Jordan and in Gaza.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: On the question of recognition of Palestine, Singapore has consistently affirmed the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and their own state.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In many instances, Singapore has voted in support of the Palestinians at the UN.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This has been our consistent position which we have maintained so far, while doing as much as we can to help strengthen the Palestinian Authority's capabilities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, we are concerned that extremist elements on both sides continue to undermine the prospects for a negotiated two-state solution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, Israeli settlers continue to displace Palestinians in the West Bank.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Some Israeli politicians have spoken about annexing parts of the West Bank or Gaza.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Israeli government recently approved the construction of the E1 settlement project in the West Bank.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This will fragment the West Bank and threaten the contiguity of Arab towns in the Occupied Palestinian Territories.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We call on the Israeli government to cease settlement construction and expansion.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore opposes ongoing attempts to create new facts on the ground which undermine the prospects for a two-state solution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Details will be announced at a later date.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore's approach to foreign policy is grounded on objective realities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Many countries, like Singapore, see the recognition of Palestine – when it has an effective government that accepts Israel's right to exist and categorically renounces terrorism – as a meaningful step towards the ultimate goal of a negotiated two-state solution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But a few countries have chosen to recognise a Palestinian State now, even as the prospects of a functioning state have become more remote.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: They do so precisely to express their grave concern at the status quo, and hope to make it harder for Israel to extinguish a two-state solution altogether.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Singapore's support for a two-state solution means that we will oppose any steps by Israel to extinguish or undermine such a solution.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It is hard to foresee how the situation in the Middle East will develop in the future.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Nevertheless, Singapore's stance will continue to be guided by our national interests, of which the maintenance of the unity and cohesion among our people is of utmost importance.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To that end, we will continue to make every effort to help Singaporeans understand the rationale for the foreign policy stance we take.
